paragraphs.text: MCF7 cells engineered to express a doxycycline (DOX)-inducible-hemagglutinin (HA)-tagged Y537S mutant ER [13] were grown in DMEM supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS), 10 µg/ml penicillin–streptomycin-glutamine (PSG) and 500 µg/ml of geneticin (full medium), either without DOX (ER-WT MCF7 cells) or with 1 µg/ml DOX to induce the expression of the Y537S ER mutation (ER-mutant MCF7 cells). This model was extensively characterized in reference 13.

DOX-untreated engineered MCF7 cells were transduced with the ClonTracer library [34], a high-complexity 30 bp-long semi-random DNA barcode library which contains ~ 73 million unique barcodes (Addgene #69830). The packaging of the library into lentiviruses and the infection of the cells were performed following the manufacturer’s instructions. Specifically, 20 million DOX-untreated MCF7 cells were infected with the ClonTracer library. To enhance virus infection, cells were maintained in full medium supplemented with 8 µg/ml of polybrene for 48 h. After transduction, the selection of the barcoded cells was performed by maintaining them in full medium supplemented with 2 µg/ml of puromycin for 96 h. In order to ensure that each cell was infected with one barcode, the multiplicity of infection (MOI) was set at 0.1. The selected barcoded cells (parental cells) were expanded for 3 passages in full medium supplemented with 1 µg/ml of puromycin and the complexity of the library was assessed by barcode sequencing. Next, the parental cells were further expanded and divided to be maintained in full medium supplemented with 1 µg/ml of puromycin, with or without DOX.

To generate three evolutionary replicates of ER-WT and ER-mutant palbociclib-resistant and abemaciclib-resistant cells, DOX-treated and untreated MCF7 cells were cultured in triplicates over time and exposed to escalating doses of the drugs (50 nM, 100 nM, 200 nM, 350 nM, 500 nM, 750 nM and 1 µM) every three passages. Cells were defined as resistant when their ability to proliferate in the presence of palbociclib or abemaciclib 1 µM was restored. Palbociclib-resistant and abemaciclib-resistant cells were regularly maintained in full medium supplemented with 1 µg/ml of puromycin, with or without DOX, and with palbociclib or abemaciclib 1 µM, respectively. In parallel, as controls, ER-WT and ER-mutant MCF7 cells were cultured in vehicle (0.01% dimethyl sulfoxide, DMSO). To ensure equal barcode representation across replicates and minimize stochastic barcode losses over time, 30 million cells were plated at every passage. To assess the barcoding library distribution over time, resistant models were sequenced at three time points: an early time point (after 3 passages in full medium with palbociclib or abemaciclib at 50 nM), an intermediate time point (after 3 passages in full medium with palbociclib or abemaciclib at 200 nM), and at the time of resistance to palbociclib or abemaciclib. Control cells were sequenced at the same timepoints.

WT-ER was overexpressed in WT-ER PalboR MCF7 cells by lentiviral transduction using a pLVX-ESR1_HA_blast plasmid (an ESR1 overexpression construct carrying a C-terminal 3 × HA tag). This plasmid was custom made by GenScript using the pLVX-IRES-puro vector. The pLVX-ESR1_HA_blast plasmid was packaged into viral particles in HEK293T cells using the pMD2.G (Addgene #12259) and psPAX (Addgene #12260) lentiviral packaging vectors. Transduced cells were selected and maintained in full medium supplemented with 5 µg/ml blasticidin for 10 days. After selection, the WT-ER palbociclib-resistant MCF7 cells overexpressing WT-ER (ER-OE PalboR MCF7 cells) were maintained in full medium supplemented with 1 µg/ml puromycin, 5 µg/ml blasticidin, and 1 µM palbociclib.

Cells were authenticated by short tandem repeat profiling (Bio-Synthesis, USA) and regularly tested for mycoplasma contamination using the MycoAlert® Mycoplasma Detection Kit (Lonza) according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

Cells were seeded in triplicate in 96-well plates (5,000 cells/well), and 24 h later (day 0) treated with palbociclib, abemaciclib, or vehicle (0.01% DMSO). At specific timepoints cells were stained with 0.4 µg/ml hoechst for nuclear staining and 4 µg/ml propidium iodide to label dead cells. The number of live and dead cells following drug treatments was counted using the Celigo image Cytometer (Nexcelom). For the IC50 studies, cells were counted at day 5 and the number of live cells was normalized against the number of cells treated with the respective drug’s vehicle. IC50 values were next calculated in Graphpad Prism using the log(inhibitor) vs. response – Variable slope (four parameters) function. For the GR metrics, cells were counted at day 0 and at day 6. GR50 and GRmax values were next calculated using the R metrics package (v1.36) (https://bioconductor.org/packages/GRmetrics/). For the growth studies, the number of live cells at different timepoints was normalized to the number of live cells counted at day 0.

Genomic DNA was extracted from 10 million cells or frozen pulverized tumors using Blood & Cell Culture DNA Kit (Qiagen). Library preparation was performed using 2 µg of genomic DNA, Titanium Taq DNA Polymerase (Takara Bio) and primers following the PCR conditions reported in Additional file 2: Table S2.

The PCR product (~ 183 bp) was purified using the QIAquick PCR purification kit (Qiagen) following the manufacturer’s protocol, quantified by Qubit dsDNA high-sensitivity assay (ThermoFisher Scientific) and sequenced at the Molecular Biology Core Facility of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute by Illumina NS500 Single-End 75 bp sequencing, using the Illumina custom primer GCGACCACCGAGATCTACACACTGACTGCAGTCTGAGTCTGACAG.

Low-frequency barcodes, defined as barcodes with fractions less than a chosen threshold fraction across all samples for models included in an analysis, were removed prior to the generation of the barcode fraction heatmaps (threshold = 0.01), the hierarchical clustering of all the bulk samples (threshold = 0.001), and the study of the dynamics of cell clusters within each condition (threshold = 0.001). These low-frequency barcodes were retained for barcode-level entropy calculations.

For barcode fraction heatmaps, Euclidean distances between barcodes (samples) were calculated on rows (columns) of the (barcodes x samples) natural-log transformed barcode fraction matrix and hierarchically clustered with complete linkage. A pseudocount of 1e-12 was added to all barcode fractions prior to log transforming for distance calculations.

Barcode distributions were compared across pairs of samples using the log2 unit Jensen-Shannon (JS) divergence using the philentropy (v0.9.0) R package [35]. Matrices of JS divergences among samples were hierarchically clustered using complete linkage. The JS divergences between samples and their respective parental control were compared across three timepoints to assess the progression of clonal selection using two-sided paired t-tests adjusted for multiple comparisons using the Holm procedure with pairing by evolutionary replicate.

Clonal selection among the barcodes at the endpoint for each sample was compared by calculating the normalized, natural-log unit Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence of the sample barcode fraction distribution against a reference discrete uniform distribution over the same number of barcodes and normalizing by the total number of barcodes using the philentropy (v0.9.0) R package [35].

Normalized KL divergences at the barcode level were compared between models using two-sided, unpaired, unequal variances t-tests using rstatix (v0.7.2) (https://doi.org/10.32614/CRAN.package.rstatix) and adjusting for multiple testing with the Holm procedure [36].

Cellular populations per model were chosen by taking the (barcode x sample) barcode fraction matrix across one parental model and all 3 timepoints (Early, Middle, End) for all 3 evolutionary replicates of a model (10 samples total) and fitting a Poisson GLM per row and extracting the Poisson Pearson residual (PPR) matrix. Euclidean distances between barcodes were calculated on rows of the PPR matrix and hierarchically clustered with complete linkage. The resulting dendrogram was cut to get 8 cellular populations per model.

Clonal selection among the 8 cellular populations at the End timepoint for each sample per condition was evaluated by calculating the normalized, natural-log KL divergence of the cellular population fraction distribution (rescaled to 1) against a reference discrete uniform distribution over 8 elements using the philentropy (v0.9.0) R package [35].

Normalized KL divergences at the cellular population level were compared between models using unpaired, t-tests with unequal variances, using rstatix (v0.7.2) (https://doi.org/10.32614/CRAN.package.rstatix), and were adjusted for multiple testing with the Holm procedure where appropriate [36].

All barcoding analyses were done in R (v4.3.2, v4.4.1) using tidyverse (v2.0.0) (https://doi.org/10.32614/CRAN.package.tidyverse) packages and readxl (v1.4.5) (https://doi.org/10.32614/CRAN.package.readxl). Plots were created in R, using ggplot2 (v3.5.2) (https://doi.org/10.32614/CRAN.package.ggplot2), RColorBrewer (v1.1–3) (https://doi.org/10.32614/CRAN.package.RColorBrewer), pheatmap (v1.0.12) (https://doi.org/10.32614/CRAN.package.pheatmap), and ggpubr (v0.6.0) (https://doi.org/10.32614/CRAN.package.ggpubr), or in GraphPad Prism (version 10.0.0).

To perform scRNA-seq analyses we used single-cell suspensions from parental cells and ER-WT and ER-mutant vehicle-control, palbociclib-resistant and abemaciclib-resistant cells. Specifically, for vehicle-control, palbociclib-resistant and abemaciclib-resistant conditions, the scRNA-seq was performed on the evolutionary replicates #3. ScRNA-seq analyses were also performed on the ER-WT palbociclib-resistant clone #3_15.

ScRNA-seq libraries were prepared at the Translational Immunogenic Lab at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, according to 10 × Genomics Chromium Next GEM Single Cell 3’ v3.1 protocol and using cell stock concentrations with a likelihood of around 8,000 transcriptomes recovering. The quality of the libraries was checked by Bioanalyzer using the High Sensitivity DNA kit (Agilent). The RNA was sequenced by Illumina HiSeq or Novaseq6000 Paired-End 150 bp sequencing at Novogene Corporation Inc.

nonexpressed_limitation.text: Our study has a few limitations. We used an engineered inducible ESR1 Y537S system enabling controlled lineage tracing, but this system cannot capture all biologically relevant selective pressures. Specifically, interactions between cancer cells and the tumor microenvironment cells are not accounted for. Future studies should extend lineage tracing to in vivo drug treatment in immune competent models. Since the barcodes in the ClonTracer library are not expressed we could not link all the enriched subpopulations with their specific transcriptional profiles. In addition, given the relatively small number of evolutionary replicates, we cannot definitively rule out the possibility that the observed convergence is influenced, at least in part, by sampling bias.
